title: Manual Review Event
description: One human-reviewed manual-intake transcription (WO-010-R4 §7). Deliberately not shaped like schemas/collection_run.schema.json -- nothing was fetched over a network, so there is no request URL, HTTP status or response content hash to record instead of these.

source_id.description: Must equal both the containing file's source_id and the filename stem; the loader checks both.

reviewed_at.description: When the human reviewer actually looked. Rejected by the loader if later than the build's as-of time.

reviewer_record.description: The named human accountable for this transcription. Never a role or team name alone.

record_count.description: How many bounded records this review produced. Never negative -- schema-enforced, not just checked in code.

related_record_ids.description: Evidence or observation record IDs this review event is the basis for. WO-010-R5 §2/R6 §2: when the loader (collectors.collection_runs.load_manual_review_events) is given the current record index, it verifies every one of these IDs itself -- each must resolve to a real, same-source, non-fixture, current-dataset record dated at or before the review, record_count must agree with how many actually do, and the event's own reviewed_record_set_sha256 must match a hash recomputed from the current record set -- rather than trusting this list, or analysis.review_package alone, to catch a bad reference. A manual review event naming none is unusual enough that callers should treat an empty list here as a signal, not silently accept it as normal.

data_cutoff_at.description: The cutoff the reviewer was working from -- e.g. 'the publisher's page as it read on this date'.

bounded_content_confirmed.description: True only if the reviewer confirms the transcribed claim is bounded (a short claim and a link), not a republished article or full page.

underlying_publisher.description: The named publisher of record. Null only permitted when the source contract's qualification.underlying_publisher_required is not true; the loader enforces this against the registry.

content_sha256.description: Hash of the authored claim record, in the same content_hash_scope sense event_evidence.schema.json uses -- never a hash standing in for a fetched publisher response.

reviewed_record_set_sha256.description: WO-010-R6 §2. Deterministic hash over canonical summaries (record_id, source_id, dataset, evidence_origin, content hash, timestamp, event_id) of every record in related_record_ids, sorted by record_id. The loader recomputes this from the current record index and rejects the event if it disagrees -- catching drift (a record's content, source or dataset changed) that an existence-only check of related_record_ids cannot.
